description: Identity-free capture() replay outcome matrix (06-02-PLAN.md D-07/D-14; must_haves truth 2). Each scenario names one required orchestration outcome/retry/equality/calendar-adjacent behavior; tests/capture/test_orchestrator.py builds the matching offline candidate/archive/clock scenario in Python (a JSON fixture cannot itself encode a mutated CSV candidate) and asserts the resulting CaptureStatus and sleeper call sequence against the documented values below -- so this document is the single source of truth a reviewer can read without also reading Python, and any accidental drift between the two fails the corresponding parametrized test.

scenarios.name: accepted_first_attempt
scenarios.narrative: A structurally valid, status-vocabulary-compliant candidate admits cleanly on the first attempt against a fresh store.

scenarios.name: terminal_rejected_structural
scenarios.narrative: A candidate with a wrong CSV header fails a structural admission check and rejects on the first attempt; never retried.

scenarios.name: empty_object_set_rejected
scenarios.narrative: A candidate missing one of the four required logical-list objects rejects before archive synchronization or the build ever run.

scenarios.name: current_date_no_new_release
scenarios.narrative: The store already has a promoted revision for the exact date this attempt expects; a byte-identical candidate is idempotent -- no_new_release stops immediately without retrying, since retrying cannot change the outcome.

scenarios.name: prior_date_no_new_release_exhaustion
scenarios.narrative: The store already has a promoted revision for a date earlier than this attempt expects (the source has not yet republished today); every attempt returns the identical prior-date no_new_release result, so all three bounded attempts retry and the loop stops only on exhaustion.

scenarios.name: prior_date_no_new_release_then_next_same_date_revision
scenarios.narrative: The first attempt repeats the already-promoted prior-date candidate (no_new_release, retried); the second attempt supplies a structurally valid, differently-fingerprinted candidate sharing the same as-of date, which admits as the next immutable revision for that date and stops the loop.

scenarios.name: transient_source_transfer_failure_then_accepted
scenarios.narrative: fetch_candidate() raises a closed transient transfer failure on the first two attempts and succeeds on the third; all three bounded attempts are used and the final outcome is accepted.

scenarios.name: persistent_source_transfer_failure_exhaustion
scenarios.narrative: fetch_candidate() raises a closed transient transfer failure on every attempt; after exhausting all three bounded attempts the call collapses to operational_error/source_transfer_error, never echoing the underlying exception detail.
